headline: A Pakistan Air Quality Initiative report released on Tuesday said Lahore's average PM2.5 from October 1 to November 9 was 126 micrograms per cubic metre, eight times the WHO guideline, with 16,714 likely crop-residue fires detected in Punjab.

card.desc: PAQI report: average PM2.5 was 126 from Oct 1 to Nov 9.

caption:
Lahore's air pollution was eight times the WHO limit!
According to Dawn, a Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) report released on Tuesday says Lahore's average PM2.5 was 126 micrograms per cubic metre from October 1 to November 9. Satellites found 16,714 likely crop-residue fires in Punjab in this period. PDMA has forecast rain in most Punjab districts for two days, which may reduce smog.
